requirement:
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
rationale: I judged this from the supplied test text only and did not request implementation source. The marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.details`. **Detail subchapter per recorded process.** - `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reports_identify_attempts_and_union_child_counts_without_discarding_profiles]` records two test attempts. It asserts that the index has four sub-items (two attempts plus their source chapters). It also asserts that each "# Test process coverage" chapter is linked from the index by `chapter_href`. **Identification fields.** - The same test asserts each detail contains `Binary: binary`, `Attempt: 1`, `Outcome: success` and a capture time. It asserts `Test: one` and `Run: {first_run}` on the detail for the first run's test. - Only the `success` outcome is asserted in a detail chapter. The `failed` and `interrupted` outcomes are exercised in `fn[filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source]`, but only the index is checked there. I treat outcome rendering as one formatted value, not a separate behavior, so this is not a gap. **Source lines and counts.** - The test above checks that the detail embeds the per-line count JSON, for example `"1":"0","2":"7"`. - `.github/scripts/coverage-viewer.test.mjs` checks the rendered viewer. It asserts `18446744073709551615 executed` and `0 unexecuted`, so executed and unexecuted lines are distinguished and large counts are preserved. It asserts the captured text `` is shown literally. It asserts that source is accepted only from the report's own iframe and run. - `fn[rendered_detail_scripts_remain_literal_across_blank_lines]` renders the chapter through pulldown-cmark. It checks that the viewer script and the count JSON survive intact. **Source captured for that run.** - After `code.rs` is rewritten, `reports_identify_attempts...` and `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` both assert the details still contain the saved `fn one() {}` source. Both also check the profiles remain. **Link back to the index.** - `reports_identify_attempts...` asserts each detail contains `[Back to coverage index](../coverage.html)`. - `fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_index_hierarchy_after_existing_children]` asserts `../coverage.html` for numbered and unnumbered parents. It also checks that the detail chapters inherit `parent_names` and section numbering. **Child coverage distinguishable.** - `reports_identify_attempts...` asserts the detail contains both `"kind":"Test"` and `"kind":"Child"` process records, and that the child's counts stay separate. - The viewer test renders a "Child process 2" section and lazily loads the child's file source on toggle. It also checks the child's source is not shown until its section is opened. All obligations have tests that assert their outcomes. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} index.details
For the records displayed by {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
`habeas mdbook` MUST generate a detail subchapter under the index chapter for
each recorded nextest test process, identifying its binary, test name, attempt,
test-attempt outcome, and originating run. Each report MUST show its instrumented
first-party Rust source lines and execution counts, distinguishing executed
from unexecuted lines, using the source captured for that run, and link back to
the index.
Coverage from associated child processes MUST remain distinguishable from
coverage recorded by the nextest test process itself.
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
